searchText: > if everyone did that we'd lose the chain history. If everyone did this then we wouldn't need chain history. 🙂 Not true - Eth2 happens to depend on that history. 🙂 In what way does ETH2 depend on chain history? It loads deposits based off the transaction receipts. I'm familiar with Nethermind not downloading that history because of the number of times people have discovered it not work with Eth2 clients. How dose ETH2 find the deposit receipts in history? with the eth_getReceipts JSON-RPC call. Eth2 clients have to have a eth1 node to read from. Doing an update on the Teku pyrmont nodes. So I'm trying to do the deposit contract and following the instructions on the launch pad The virtual env commands failed and then the PIP3 install requirements through some errors about keys not matching What am I doing wrong this deposit client stepped didn't give any hiccups when I did it on nimbus or tekku versions and I don't remember this install virtual env <@340345049063882753> you can configure nethermind to just download receipts from deposit contract onwards. With that config ,you can find all deposits with eth1 node that takes only 100GB. Although I noticed, state has grown 25gb on disk in last couple of days which is worrying Yes my concern is that the default config is a selfish setting. Nethermind only gets away with it because it’s not a majority client. If geth were to take the same policy it would become extremely difficult to find that historic data.
